lines: The SPPD has been investigating a gang planning to smuggle drugs into prison with an armored car. <Col: StageText>Prevent</Col> the theft of this <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col> by Criminals.

Dr. Borious needs your help moving prescription drugs to our brothers in prison. <Col: StageText>Break into</Col> a <Col: StageText>security truck</Col> - our SPPD contact will use it to drive the drugs past prison security.
Now they have the armored car, the gang is planning to bomb a pharmacy and steal prescription drugs. <Col: StageText>Protect</Col> this <Col: StageText>drug store</Col> from the Criminals.

Next step: get the drugs. The pharmacy we'll hit is pretty big on security - the windows are reinforced. <Col: StageText>Bomb</Col> the <Col: StageText>pharmacy</Col> to get access to the drugs inside.
The gang is searching for more drugs in the pharmacy's secure storage area. <Col: StageText>Protect</Col> the storage area's <Col: StageText>door</Col> from the Criminals.

Dr. Borious found where the pharmacy keeps the specialty drugs requested by our imprisoned gang members. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col> the pharmacy's secure storage area and <Col: StageText>pick up</Col> the medication.

A dirty cop plans to deliver the drugs by driving the van into the prison. <Col: StageText>Prevent</Col> the Criminals from <Col: StageText>dropping off</Col> the van and prescription drugs to their driver. He's at this SPPD <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>.

It won't be easy dropping that truck in to the SPPD without getting noticed, but that's why we pay you the big bucks. <Col: StageText>Deliver</Col> the drugs and the security truck to the SPPD's <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>.

The gang dropped the drugs at the police lockup, but the SPPD driver was a no-show - he saw us coming. <Col: StageText>Take down</Col> the gang's <Col: StageText>leader</Col> - we want to get the name of that dirty officer.

The medication is on its way to the prison, but an Enforcer ID'd your leader as an associate of Dr. Borious. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader</Col> and kill the Enforcers, or they'll uncover the drug transfer!

Shin Spade, PI, has been investigating Criminal mastermind Terence Piper, and sent his findings to the police. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>mailboxes </Col>from Criminals trying to destroy the evidence.

Shin Spade, a private dick, dug up some dirt on Terence Piper - friend to Crims everywhere - and sent it to SPPD Commissioner Thirly. <Col: StageText>Bomb </Col>these <Col: StageText>mailboxes </Col>to destroy them.

Criminals have destroyed two out of the five packages that contain secret files on Terence Piper. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these two <Col: StageText>mailboxes </Col>that contain more of the files.

Nice work. Spade has dug up some stories linking Piper to various criminal organizations, including us. <Col: StageText>Bomb </Col>these two <Col: StageText>mailboxes </Col>to destroy more of his evidence.

Shin Spade has given us the location of the last package of evidence so we can protect it. This is our only chance to get real, solid dirt on Piper! <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>box </Col>before the Criminals do.

Shin Spade thought we might intercept the mail, so he hid the last package of evidence and notified the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>box </Col>before the Enforcers take it to their lockup.
<Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the box at our <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>and keep it away from the Criminals. This evidence could link Piper to every gang in San Paro!
Keep the package of files away from the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Drop it off </Col>at our <Col: StageText>safe house</Col>. You don't want to end up on the wrong side of Terence Piper.
<Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the box at our <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>and keep it away from the Criminals. This evidence could link Piper to every gang in San Paro!
Keep the package of files away from the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Drop it off </Col>at our <Col: StageText>safe house</Col>. You don't want to end up on the wrong side of Terence Piper.

Since the Cexis company showed off their tech at the Games Industry Expo, they've had problems with industrial spies. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>containing their motion controller prototypes.

TOSHIO contracted us to steal technology from a tech research company, for their 'Gameport 4' console. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>this researcher's <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and steal the motion controller prototypes.

Industrial spies are targeting the Cexis company's offices. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>and prevent theft of the research files for their motion controllers being stored there.

The research company's office has blueprints: <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>and retrieve the <Col: StageText>files </Col>there. I guess we're doing this because TOSHIO couldn't buy the company out. That's business for you.
Several files, including blueprints of the Cexis company's prototype motion controller technology, were stolen. <Col: StageText>Prevent delivery </Col>of those files at all costs.

Good work. Now <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>files and prototypes </Col>at one of our hideouts and we'll do the rest. Who'd have thought the games industry was so cutthroat? Oh well, hopefully it pays well!
We've lost track of the files; they're a lost cause now. <Col: StageText>Kill or arrest the leader </Col>of the industrial spies instead. Use any means necessary.
Looks like some Enforcers picked up your trail while you were fulfilling our contract. <Col: StageText>Take them out</Col> and <Col: StageText>protect your leader </Col>- they're out for blood...

An SPPD cop went missing while working undercover in the Gs. Carter has asked us to investigate. We found the cop's car: <Col: StageText>protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>until the SPPD can come for it.

Orders from Big Daddy Arlon: Green Planet is due in court for supplying us with guns and the law has a strong case against them. <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>to the <Col: StageText>prosecutor's car </Col>and steal evidence.
The G-Kings ran off with the contents of the missing cop's car. We traced their movements to this lockup. <Col: StageText>Protect the building </Col>and prevent theft of further clues.

Files are also kept at the prosecutor's lockup. <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>and <Col: StageText>retrieve the files</Col>. You know they call him the "demon prosecutor"? Until now he's never failed to get a 'guilty' verdict!
The G-Kings have evidence we can use to locate the missing SPPD officer. <Col: StageText>Prevent delivery </Col>of those items. We can't afford to look bad in front of the SPPD!

Nice. Now <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>files </Col>at our hideout to dispose of them. With that done, Green Planet's attorney can easily rip apart what's left of the prosecution's case.

Those G-Kings destroyed the evidence leading to the missing officer. They likely saw through his cover and killed him; they're notoriously hard to infiltrate. <Col: StageText>Kill or arrest the crew's leader.</Col>

The "demon prosecutor" has some dim-witted detectives out, trying to locate the files you stole. Make sure the only thing they find is a messy death: <Col: StageText>kill them</Col> and <Col: StageText>protect your leader.</Col>

Our attempt to ambush Jeung Bloodrose ended in complete disaster. Find our <Col: StageText>surveillance van </Col>and <Col: StageText>prevent Blood Roses </Col>from <Col: StageText>breaking in</Col>; we need the data from the van to know what happened.

Twizzy, a wealthy but paranoid blogger, has been slamming Charlotte's fashion sense. Big mistake. <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>to this <Col: StageText>van </Col>and grab the kit needed to nudge her mansion's electro-mechanical locks.

The Blood Roses are taking shit from the strike teams they wipe out. That's prime equipment; we can't let them have it. Find the equipment and <Col: StageText>prevent the Roses </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking it up</col>.

We need security tags to bypass Twizzy's door security. Luckily a friend got us some. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>tags</Col>. Too bad Twizzy doesn't have pets or we could've mailed them to her, in bits, instead.

Of the strike teams we sent to ambush Jeung, only one survivor was seen... leaving with a briefcase. A bribe? He's a corpse now, but the case is missing. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the Roses from <Col: StageText>picking it up</col>.

The last bit of gear we need is an <Col: StageText>image-neutralizing system </Col>to remotely disable Twizzy's security cameras. Go <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>the system and bring it back here, with everything else.

The Blood Roses hold all the answers to the mysteries behind our failed ambush on Jeung. <Col: StageText>Don't let the Roses </Col>get those items to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We can't let this go unsolved.
Good, good. <Col: StageText>Drop off the whole lot </Col>at the hideout and we'll be all set for 'Operation Kiss Charlotte's Ass' later tonight. That silly Twizzy bitch won't even see us coming.
All the evidence we could've used to piece this event together is beyond our reach now. All we can do is get revenge for our fallen. <Col: StageText>Kill or arrest the leader</Col>.

Twizzy's fan club seems to have got wind of our little game. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader </Col> and <Col: StageText>kill </Col>any fans who come after you: they'll just be trouble later, if we let them live.

A smuggling operation we've been tracking took a big delivery, but before we could raid them, the G-Kings turned up. Find one of the <Col: StageText>smuggler's vans </Col>and <Col: StageText>prevent the Gs </Col>from <Col: StageText>breaking in </Col>to it.

Veronika just gave me a call saying her crew spotted Prentiss Tigers moving weapons through here: real top-grade stuff like OCAs and Somatics. <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>to this <Col: StageText>van </Col>and grab the guns.

The G-Kings have sent the smugglers running. We need some of the smuggled merchandise to give us a lead on their organization. Find the merch and <Col: StageText>prevent the Gs </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking it up</col>.

The Tigers high-tailed it with the rest. They were too wounded to carry the guns far, so they'll have them stashed somewhere. Find and <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>boxes </Col>those shiny guns are in.

Looks like we weren't the only ones tracking this smuggling deal; the G-Kings are trying to steal the money that was to be used as payment. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the G-Kings from <Col: StageText>picking it up</col>.

Hey, whaddya know: found me some corpses with paperwork. Says here the last part of the Tiger shipment was a custom sniper rifle. Go <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>the rifle and bring it back with everything else.

All the evidence we need to pursue our smuggling case is being whisked away by those G-Kings! <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>those dirtbags from <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>their haul. We can't let this operation go to waste.
Nice one! We've got ourselves some new toys and a whole bunch of Tigers are now fertilizer. <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>those bullet-spitters at the hideout and watch out for trouble.
The whole smuggling operation is a bust. The G-Kings have robbed us of all our potential leads! <Col: StageText>Kill or arrest their leader</Col>.

Looks like we need weed killer; the Prentiss Tigers are back! New guys, that is, not the dead ones. The only zombie you'll find round here is our mohawked mascot. <Col: StageText>Kill them</Col> and <Col: StageText>protect your leader</Col>.
We've figured out where Pagan Bloodrose keeps her ill-gotten gains. Roses are trying to clear the place out before we can get there. <Col: StageText>Stop them breaking in </Col>and taking the money.

Pagan is stuck at a restaurant with her family. Her uncle, Commissioner of the SPPD, is asking awkward questions. Do Pagan a favor and <Col: StageText>break in </Col>to where she keeps her Blood Rose cash and remove it.
The Roses made off with Pagan Bloodrose's dirty money before we could get a warrant to search the stash house. <Col: StageText>Prevent them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering it </Col>to her.
Good work. Pagan wouldn't want all those hard-earned dollars falling into the right hands. <Col: StageText>Drop them off </Col>near the restaurant; she'll come out and pick them up later.

Pagan Bloodrose knows we're onto her; she's looking to cause a major distraction as a decoy. <Col: StageText>Protect these buildings </Col>from being torched. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>anyone who tries to stop you.

Pagan is getting grilled by her Uncle, Commissioner Carter. Create an emergency for him to have to deal with. <Col: StageText>Burn these businesses, </Col>but <Col: StageText>avoid getting killed</Col>: that'd only raise further questions.
Those fires aren't the Commissioner's problem but Criminals openly causing havoc would be cause for concern. Keep them out of this area before people start panicking.

Those fires aren't cutting it. Get out there and make your presence known by <Col: StageText>controlling this area</Col>. Some Enforcer bloodshed will give Comissioner Carter something other'n Pagan to worry about.
The G-Kings have been called in to recover a debt for a local restaurant. <Col: StageText>Stop the G-Kings </Col>from <Col: StageText>breaking into the office </Col>of the alleged debtors.

Terri Quan is good friends with TV chef Rick Shank. A company has refused to pay their bill at Rick's restaurant. <Col: StageText>Break into their offices </Col>and <Col: StageText>take </Col>what they owe. And get a tip too.
The G-Kings have looted over $5000 and are delivering it the restaurant that hired them to steal it. <Col: StageText>Prevent the Gs </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the money</Col>.
<Col: StageText>Drop off the payment </Col>next to Rick's resturant. He'll come out and pick it up later, so we aren't connected. Any friend of Terri's...

To conceal where and when they will drop off the cash to the restaurant, the G-Kings're planning a distraction. <Col: StageText>Protect these buildings </Col>from being torched. <Col: StageText>Kill anyone </Col>who gets in the way.

To make sure no one is around to see Rick picking up the money, go create a G-King style ruckus. <Col: StageText>Burn these businesses, </Col>but <Col: StageText>avoid getting killed</Col>; Rick is a strict vegetarian.
Those fires aren't big enough for a distraction and looks like these Criminals are eager for a bigger distraction. Keep them out of this area before they incite mass panic.
Rick Shank's being kinda paranoid and wants more of a distraction than just a few housefires. Get out there and make your presence known by <Col: StageText>controlling this area.</Col>
The Praetorians are trying to look vaguely competent in front of the press by kicking down our doors. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>raiding</Col> our businesses.
Some of the City Council don't like seeing Praetorians on the streets. Prove to them we can tackle the drug problem. <Col: StageText>Raid these drug operations</Col> to demonstrate our effectiveness.
The Praetorians are trying to prove to the press how tough they are. Embarrass them. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding</Col> our businesses.
They must have been tipped off. The place was empty, aside from some passed-out junkies. New intel points to a second location you need to check out. <Col: StageText>Raid this building</Col>.
We've loaded up our supplies so the Praetorians won't find them when they raid our properties. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching our cars </Col>until we move out.
A guy from the first place you busted confessed that there is a stash of drugs in two nearby cars. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the drugs</Col> from the cars.
The Praetorians have got our car, with our supplies in the trunk. <Col: StageText>Prevent them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering it</Col> back to their lockup.
Good work. <Col: StageText>Drop off the drugs</Col> at the lockup. Hea Choi says this bust will make us look good at our next press conference.
The Praetorians are going to keep disrupting our operations unless we can stop them, permanently. <Col: StageText>Take out their leader</Col>.

These Criminals aren't happy about you raiding their drug operation. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader </Col> while trying to <Col: StageText>kill or arrest them</Col>, so they can't re-open for business.
The Tigers are out trying to impress their mommies again. Adorable. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the brats from <Col: StageText>raiding our business</Col>.
Some of the City Council don't like the whole Prentiss Tiger vibe. <Col: StageText>Raid these drug operations</Col> and show the squares how we play it.

The Tigers are on a PR mission to prove their street smarts - yeah, right! Let's kick their asses while they stand around posing. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding our businesses</Col>.
They must've heard we were coming; the place was emptier than the Tiger's chess club. We have a second location. <Col: StageText>Raid the building</Col>.
We've loaded up our supplies so the Tigers won't find them during their raids. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching our cars </Col>until we can move 'em out.
Pick up those drugs. The rest appear to have been loaded up into vehicles so they can be shipped out. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the drugs </Col>from these two cars.
The Tigers got our cars with the supplies in the trunk, the joy-riding bastards. <Col: StageText>Prevent them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering our supplies </Col>back to their frat house.
Nice job! <Col: StageText>Drop off the drugs</Col> at the lockup. This bust will definitely make us look awesome on the TV. Wave to your mom. I will be.
The Tigers are going to keep on pissing in our punchbowl unless we stop them, permanently. <Col: StageText>Take out their leader</Col>!

These Criminals aren't happy about you spoiling their drug party. <Col: StageText>Kill or arrest them</Col> or they'll keep coming back - like herpes. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader </Col>, they'll be gunning for their head.

Get over to this shipping center - we had explosives imported into the city but Enforcers are coming to confiscate them. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching this crate</Col>.

Head to this shipping center: we've intercepted communications about explosives being shipped into the city - and without help from the Blood Roses, for once. <Col: StageText>Search this crate </Col>for any contraband.

Enforcers have confiscated explosives from one of the crates we had shipped into the city. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>the explosives at their lockup facility.

Yeah, those explosives are Somatic XAGs; definitely not for demolition work of any legal kind. Confiscate the explosives and <Col: StageText>drop them off </Col>at the <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>facility.

One of our shipments has already been seized and Enforcers are going to check our other shipments for explosive devices. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching this crate</Col>.

Kamotsu Imports shipped the crates you just seized. We checked with them and there were more containers from this shipment sent around the city. <Col: StageText>Check this crate </Col>for any more explosives.
<Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>before they <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the explosives at their lockup facility. <Col:StageText> Grab the Explosives</Col> and take them to the dead drop.

Whoa! Those are Somatic's highest-grade explosives. Good thing you got to them before they hit the streets. Confiscate them and <Col: StageText>drop them off </Col>at the <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>facility.
<Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>before they <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the explosives at their lockup facility. <Col:StageText> Grab the Explosives</Col> and take them to the dead drop.

One of our crew - Alonzo - just got busted by the D.A. and the 'Torians are going to confiscate items from his home. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians</Col> from finding anything that will incriminate us.

A Trexxon exec vanished after it was discovered he was embezzling from the company. Trexxon has asked us to recoup the loss from the employee's assets; start by <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>the <Col: StageText>exec's lockup</Col>.

There is information on some of our businesses in Alonzo's cars. Praetorians are heading to impound them. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars</Col>.
The exec's cars are nearby; flashy Sungnyemun Moirais. <Col: StageText>Pick up the cars</Col>; they're to be sent back to the company. Take the stuff from the lockup with you.
Praetorians have raided Alonzo's hideouts and taken his cars for impounding. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the evidence </Col>from the hideouts to the lockup.

Before you deliver the cars, <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>exec's assets </Col>from the lockup. Millions of dollars' worth of possessions, in such small boxes; the exec's watch alone probably cost more than my house.

The Praetorians haven't realized that the cars they've seized hold important evidence. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the cars </Col>to the impound lot where it'll be thoroughly searched.
I always wanted a car like the Moirai... Though the Praetorians pay well, that car matches Justin Teng's paygrade more than mine. <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars </Col>here.
The Praetorians have found some incriminating evidence in Alonzo's confiscated possessions. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the evidence </Col>to the D.A.'s office.
The cars contained some evidence of drug use. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>criminal evidence </Col>found in the cars and <Col: StageText>drop it off </Col>at the lockup facility.
These Praetorians really think they can stop us by taking down just one member of our crew...? Make them pay for messing with us, <Col: StageText>takeout their leader</Col>.

Looks like the ex-exec is still around, and used some of his embezzlement money to hire some muscle. Guess he wants his stuff back. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader</Col> while you <Col: StageText>get rid of these scum.</Col>
We just ambushed a CUP politician - one of Mayor Derren's party. Left him with nothing but his striped boxers. Now their Enforcers are out to retrieve his things; <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>!

Just got a call: the Prentiss Rifleman's Club had a break-in and some firearms were stolen. Ballsy stuff. We've promised to get the guns back, so start off by <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>this <Col: StageText>thief's home</Col>.

The Enforcers are out to retrieve the politician's stolen Sungnyemun Moirais now. I've grown rather attached to them, though so <Col: StageText>stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars</Col>.
The thief was seen moving rifles to a set of cars nearby: Sungnyemun Moirais. <Col: StageText>Pick up the cars </Col>so we can check them for firearms. Take stuff from the thief's home with you, too.

As unattractive as it is having the politician we robbed waddle around in his underwear, it's better he stay that way. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the politician's things </Col>to their lockup.
Before you deliver the cars, <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>box of firearms </Col>from the thief's home.

The Enforcers still need to take the politician's shiny Sungnyemun Moirais to safety. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the cars </Col>to the impound lot; I want those Moirais!

The Moirais you're driving are too expensive for a lowly thief; I'm guessing the Blood Roses had a hand in this. <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars </Col>here and we'll get a forensic team on it.

Seems the politician had some papers regarding CSA policy in the car. We have friends who could use those... <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Enforcers from <Col: StageText>delivering the papers </Col>back to the politician.

The cars contained documents detailing a Blood Rose op: filing the serial numbers off stolen guns and reselling them. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>documents </Col>found in the cars and <Col: StageText>drop them off </Col>at our lockup.
The Enforcers have done an annoyingly good job of ruining our fun and making you look bad. If you <Col: StageText>takeout their squad leader</Col> though, I'll forgive you. Maybe.
The gun thieves look like they want a fight; they're back and armed with Blood Rose weaponry. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader</Col> while you <Col: StageText>get rid of these scum.</Col>
The Praetorians are trying to <Col: StageText>recover </Col>a shipment of <Col: StageText>EMP weaponry </Col>we hijacked. Use your more conventional weapons to <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.

OCA reported a shipment of prototype <Col: StageText>HPM Devices </Col>missing; we're talking serious EMP weaponry here. We traced the prototypes to this location; <Col: StageText>retrieve </Col>the devices from these <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>. ASAP.
The Praetorians have already recovered half of the arms shipment we lifted, <Col: StageText>stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the rest of the EMP weapons</Col>.

We've found a few more of the missing <Col: StageText>HPM Devices </Col>in these <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>retrieve them </Col>and make sure you don't set any off; they fire beams that fry the electronics in everything they touch.
The Praetorians have the last of the <Col: StageText>EMP weaponry</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering </Col>the shipment back to their lockup.

Nice work! <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>HPM Devices </Col>at our lockup. I'm glad we found them; in the wrong hands they could decimate security systems, kill vehicles or fry comms in mere seconds.
These Praetorians think they can just take our weaponry? <Col: StageText>Take out their leader </Col>to show them who really runs things around here.
We've got the HPM Devices secured, but it doesn't look we're out of the woods yet; the outfit that stole them are looking for their stolen goods. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader.</Col>
The Prentiss Tigers are trying to retrieve some surveillance equipment we stole. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding our car</Col>.

I don't know if you've met Nora or not - a fellow Tiger. She lent us some <Col: StageText>surveillance equipment </Col>from her father's stores, but now it's been stolen. Go <Col: StageText>retrieve it </Col>from these <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>.

The Tigers are after the remaining stolen <Col: StageText>surveillance equipment</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>van </Col>we're using to move the equipment; last thing we need is their dirty paw-marks all over it.

There's more <Col: StageText>surveillance equipment </Col>in these <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>retrieve it</Col>. If Nora knew it had been stolen, she'd be out with her minigun! Interesting to watch, but the collateral damage...
The Tigers are running off with the stolen <Col: StageText>surveillance equipment </Col>The nerve! <Col: StageText>stop them </Col>from getting the equipment to their <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>.

Good Job! <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>Nora's <Col: StageText>surveillance equipment </Col>at our lockup. It's a good thing she's visiting Fourche Bank right now; this way she doesn't even have to know it's gone missing.
The Tigers got the stolen equipment and messed up two of our vans; we can't stand for that! <Col: StageText>Take out their leader</Col>. It'll go some way towards making up for them screwing us over.
We've tracked down the Blood Roses who managed to steal Nora's surveillance equipment. We might have the equipment back, but they'll be coming for payback. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader.</Col>

Stores have been colluding with drug companies to screw customers into buying expensive medicine. We've planted bombs in front of two drugstores. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>finding </Col>them.

Bomb threats have been made against some local <Col: StageText>drugstores </Col>that have been selling an anti-gang pepper spray called 'Gangrenous'. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>the targets thoroughly.

Enforcers found the bombs we planted in front of those corrupt drugstores. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>defusing </Col>the bombs. The 'Forcers are helping to prop up these corrupt pharmaceutical companies.
These bombs are well-hidden: they're actually fitted under the sidewalk slabs! <Col: StageText>Defuse the bombs </Col>and let these drugstores continue stocking the pro-'Forcer pepper spray.

We've already planted some hidden bombs near the HQs of the drug companies. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the corporate puppet <Col: StageText>Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching </Col>for the <Col: StageText>bombs</Col>.
Makers of the 'Gangrenous' pepper spray are going to be holding a large publicity event soon. Get over there and <Col: StageText>investigate the area </Col>for possible sabotage before they set up.
A bomb we planted outside the corrupt pharmaceutical company has been found by Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>defusing </Col>the bomb and examining it for clues.
It's another one of those slim-line IEDs. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col>. Pick it up when it's been made safe; obviously, we need to gain a better understanding of this dangerous new device.

To distract Enforcers from investigating the previous bombing, we planted another IED. They're in such a panic their whole investigation into our bombs might unravel - or so we hope. <Col: StageText>Stop them searching for the bomb</Col>.

We're closing in on the gang responsible for this new bomb design. Meanwhile, <Col: StageText>search the area </Col>where 'Gangrenous' are going to be holding product demonstrations. Hidden bombs could be there too.

One of our guys has been getting sloppy with the bomb-planting and forgot to wear gloves. <Col: StageText>Stop this squad </Col>from <Col: StageText>defusing </Col>the bomb and recovering it for fingerprints.
These bombs are almost invisible. I wonder how they get the profile so thin. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb </Col>and keep it safe. We need to get a closer look.

Enough of our bombs have been recovered for the Enforcers to be able to trace them back to us. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>our bombs to their forensics <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>.
Now <Col: StageText>drop off </Col>the defused <Col: StageText>bombs </Col>you've found to the nearby <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. We'll examine them carefully and find out what makes them tick.
I'm sick of these Enforcers propping up corrupt drug companies. <Col: StageText>Defend the bomb </Col>I planted in this public area to highlight their ruthless disregard for people's health.
The gang want to set off another of their stealth bombs near the location of a big 'Gangrenous' pepper spray publicity shindig. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>bombing </Col>.
These street corners belong to some drug dealing friends of ours who pay us to provide security. They've recently seen the Praetorians patrolling. <Col: StageText>Keep the Praetorians out</Col>.
Praetorian high command needs some quick wins for our anti-drug campaign. <Col: StageText>Search this neighborhood. </Col>The stats show a high level of drug dealing in the area.

The Praetorians have found out about the local drug drop-off point and have been searching for it. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up</Col> anything our dealer friends have stashed.
The campaign is working. An informant saw your patrol and has given us the location of a drug stash. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the drugs</Col>.
Tragic! The Praetorians found the drug drop-off point and confiscated the stash. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from  <Col: StageText>seizing </Col>any more or we could lose the dealers as clients.
Better move quick: those dealers have another distribution point. <Col: StageText>Retrieve </Col>their secondary stash of <Col: StageText>drugs</Col>.

The Praetorians have searched all the drop-off points in this area and seized the drugs. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering </Col>it to their <Col: StageText>lockup.</Col>
Clean work out there. Now <Col: StageText>transfer the drugs </Col>to our facility.
The Praetorians seized our client's goods. They are not happy. Make sure the Praetorians can never do this again. <Col: StageText>Take out their leader.</Col>
The anti-drug campaign is working. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader </Col> some dealers are looking to show how pissed off they are!

These street corners belong to some drug dealing friends of ours who pay us to provide security. We hear the Prentiss Tigers have suddenly got heavy in this neighborhood. <Col: StageText>Keep them out</Col> by making it too dangerous for them to stick around.
Byeong Lee wants us to <Col: StageText>go</Col> and to make our presence felt. This <Col: StageText>neighborhood</Col> is making a ton of complaints that drug dealing is going down.
Those Prentiss frat boys found out about the local drug drop-off points and have been searching them. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up</Col> the stash.
Byeong was right. Some dudes saw you around and tipped us off where a drop point is. Get out there and <Col: StageText>snatch the drugs</Col>.
Are the Tigers planning a party? They've got half of the drug supply for this area already! <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>any more of our client's product.
This reminds me of what Coach Patchings used to say about locker searches: find one stash and it points to the next one. Go and <Col: StageText>retrieve the drugs</Col>.

It's not too late to recover our reputation with the client. I know where the Tigers' local lockup is. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the drugs </Col>and we are back in favor.
Time for a race to the end zone: <Col: StageText>drop off the drugs </Col>at our lockup.
We've got one last chance to resolve this matter for our clients and eliminate the problem at source. <Col: StageText>Take their leader out.</Col>
All right! Seems like the dirty dealers want to make a fight out of it. Suits me. <Col: StageText>Protect your leader </Col> and <Col: StageText>arrest them or take them out.</Col> Game on!

Enforcers are picking up an encrypted PDA that contains orders for their next covert mission. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the PDA </Col>and we can stop their mission before it starts.
Due to the sensitive nature of this task, your briefing will be given in the field. Move out and <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>encrypted PDA</Col>.

As part of 'Operation Killjoy', the Enforcer's are planning to eliminate gang leaders. Their first objective is to retrieve various case files. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers searching the cars for files</Col>.

A deep cover informant within the Blood Roses has compiled detailed files on several key figures. <Col: StageText>Search for </Col>the <Col: StageText>files </Col>left in these <Col: StageText>cars</Col>.
That covert team is picking up a sniper rifle and various targets' bios. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>retrieving the assassination kit</Col>.

Another set of <Col: StageText>files </Col>have been left for <Col: StageText>retrieval </Col>; raid this <Col: StageText>address</Col> to get at them. The longer these files are left out, the more chance there is of them falling into the wrong hands.

<Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Enforcers from <Col: StageText>getting </Col>the <Col: StageText>assassination kit </Col>back <Col: StageText>to their lockup</Col>. That rifle and target information could be used to take out some of our high-ranking members.
You've gathered all the files left by our Blood Rose informant. <Col: StageText>Drop everything off </Col>here. Make sure you're not followed.

We lost track of the assassination kit, but we can still <Col: StageText>take out </Col>the Enforcer <Col: StageText>group leader </Col>- that's the government spook who's going to pull the trigger for those assassinations.

You've gathered enough evidence to put away quite a few Blood Rose gang members. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>your squad <Col: StageText>leader </Col>until you can <Col: StageText>kill off the enemies </Col>out to silence you.
The Praetorians are <Col: StageText>picking up an ambulance</Col> to recover our cache of blackmarket organs. The doc ain't happy. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from mobilizing.
A Praetorian informant has discovered some human organs being sold on the black market. We'll intercept them. First step - <Col: StageText>collect</Col> an <Col: StageText>ambulance.</Col>
Praetorian Enforcers are <Col: StageText>seizing </Col> our <Col: StageText>organs</Col>. The doc wants you to <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>. It took him ages to hack them out.
Now you're in possession of the ambulance, go <Col: StageText>pick up</Col> the <Col: StageText>organs</col> so they can't be sold.

The Praetorians are <Col: StageText>taking</Col> the doc's high value <Col: StageText>organs</col> to be destroyed. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> before they get to where they're going. Unless you want to supply the replacements!

<Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>organs </Col>at this <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>with a cold storage facility. We'll have the forensics team pick them up later and expose the doctor responsible.
This isn't good - the Praetorians are trashing our organ trade. <Col: StageText>Stop them delivering </Col>the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> so they can't use it again.
Clean work. Now <Col: StageText>drop off</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>; it's still city property, you know.
The Praetorians could be on to our whole organ trafficking network. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up our latest shipment</Col>.

A second batch of organs has been found but these appear to be animal parts. We've made the traffickers desperate to close a sale. <Col: StageText>Pick up the organs</Col> before they can hit the black market.
Make or break! The Praetorians could shut down our whole organ trafficking operation with that evidence. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering</Col> it to their warehouse.
<Col: StageText>Deliver these organs</Col> to our lockup. We will destroy them before someone gets a pig's heart sewn inside them.
<Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> these organs, harvested from an escaped orangutan, before Enforcers can get their hands on them. Dr. Borious will pay good money for this mad scientist shit.
A set of organs from a recently escaped orangutan were found in transit. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> the organs before the gang get them to that Crim, Dr. Borious.

Some dickhead tried to sell our latest shipment of organs to a doctor who is loyal to the Prentiss Tigers. He is turning the organs in. <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> the Tigers from <Col: StageText>picking up</Col> the transfer <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>.
The official Tigers M.D. has confiscated some black market organs he was offered. But you don't want blood all over your ride. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> an <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> first.
The Tigers are on their way to <Col: StageText>confiscate</Col> our shipment of <Col: StageText>organs</Col>. Make sure you <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.
Nice wheels you got now buddy! The Doc has left the human spare parts out for us to collect. So go <Col: StageText>pick up</Col> the <Col: StageText>organs</col>.
The Tigers have seized our shipment of <Col: StageText>organs</col> and are <Col: StageText>dropping them off </Col>to their forensics team. <Col: StageText>Stop the transfer</Col>.

Hey, you got guts. Literally. Ha ha.  <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>organs </Col>at this <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. Forensics will deal with them there. Don't want them stinking up the place back here.
That meat wagon has to go. Make sure the <Col: StageText>ambulance </Col>doesn't get <Col: StageText>dropped off </Col>and put back into service.
It's not cool to be seen driving that wreck. Probably smells like a meat counter too. So <Col: StageText>drop off</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>.

We had to think fast for our 'budget' transplant patients and get a shipment of animal organs instead. But the Prentiss Tigers are onto us and monkey hearts don't cost peanuts you know!. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>collecting </Col> the organs.

Gross! Doc uncovered more organs, but they appear to be animal parts. We need to get them before some kid ends up shitting through a baboon's anus. <Col: StageText>Pick up the organs</Col> so we can get rid of them.
The Tigers could halt our trade in animal organs with all the evidence they have. <Col: StageText>Prevent them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering</Col> those monkey tickers.
<Col: StageText>Deliver those organs</Col> to our lockup. We've found a legitimate buyer for them. Just... don't buy any oxtail soup for a while, yeah?
<Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> these organs, harvested from an escaped orangutan, before Enforcers can get their hands on them. Dr. Borious will pay good money for this mad scientist shit.
A set of organs from a recently escaped orangutan were found in transit. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> the organs before the gang get them to that Crim, Dr. Borious.

Tigers are giving us grief over in Midtown. I'm creating a distraction here by hacking into alarm systems and setting them off. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating </Col>the alarmed properties and discovering what I'm up to.
<Col: StageText>Investigate</Col> this property. A high number of burglar alarms have been going off in that neighborhood lately.
The security alarm I set off is distracting the Prentiss Tigers. Don't let them find out it's been hacked. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>investigating</Col> the alarms.
We've just had another alarm go off. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>this one and try to catch the burglar red-handed.
It's fun to watch those Tigers run around chasing their tails. Keep them clueless. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating</Col> the rigged alarms.
The bells, the bells! Another alarm is going off... this can't be a coincidence. <Col: StageText>Force your way inside</Col> and check the place out: something funky is going down.

For a bunch of jocks, those Tigers sure are killjoys. They found out how I've been remotely rigging their security alarms. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>disabling </Col>the uplink <Col: StageText>antenna</Col> I used.
Someone is hacking into the alarm systems and setting them off, probably to make sure they keep Tigers off their tail elsewhere. <Col: StageText>Sabotage this antenna </Col>and disconnect them.

The Tigers disabled all my security alarm distractions and tracked down the hardware I was using. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the hard drive</Col> from the laptop I used for the programming.
Good work, you've taken the nerds offline. We've tracked the laptop they've been using to hack the alarm systems. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the hard drive</Col> from it.

The laptop I used to hack the security systems has been confiscated by the Prentiss Tigers. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering the hard drive</Col> to their lockup and bring it back to me.
<Col: StageText>Deliver that hard drive </Col>to the lockup. Its cache will tell us who did this and how. Plus, we can see what websites they look at, the dirty bastards.

The laptop I used to hack the security systems has been confiscated by the Prentiss Tigers. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering the hard drive</Col> to their lockup and bring it back to me.

What the hell? Every time the Praetorians go looking for news coverage, they pick on us. They're going to <Col: StageText>raid </Col>some of our <Col: StageText>phone hacking dens</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.
Most of San Paro's live TV Networks think the Praetorians are corporate and boring. <Col: StageText>Raid this drug factory </Col>and show the press just how exciting our methods can be.

The Praetorians really don't encourage you to make a profit in this town. They're going to <Col: StageText>raid </Col>more of our <Col: StageText>phone hacking dens</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.

Good job! We're getting some good cross-channel coverage after pillaging that drug factory. Now <Col: StageText>raid </Col>this <Col: StageText>drug den.</Col> The use of extreme violence is encouraged.

I keep saying: "don't leave the shit in the cars!" So guess what? The Praetorians found a shipment of <Col: StageText>modified SIMs </Col>hidden in one of our courier's vehicles. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from getting to it!

The Networks love what they're seeing. You look awesome in slow-mo! A nearby <Col: StageText>car </Col>was used by the dealers to transport the drugs. <Col: StageText>Retrieve any drugs </Col>it contains.

The Praetorians have recovered enough illegal phone numbers to get us all convicted. Unless you want to be implicated, <Col: StageText>stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping those SIMs off</Col>.
<Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>you recovered. This much dope should get convictions for the criminals - and secure us a bunch of prime-time news slots.

Our humiliation is all over TV. We could just stay in with a can of Tyler and watch our phone-hacking empire go up in flames, or we could <Col: StageText>blow up</Col> these pissant Praetorian scumbags!

Nice job - the Praetorians are headline news. Unfortunately the dealers we pissed off want some prime-time coverage of their own. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>planting bombs</Col> in the area.

The Tigers just found $800k in one of our bank accounts. It's from our diamond smuggling operation. Buy us time. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>those Prentiss pussies from <Col: StageText>raiding our accountant's office</Col>.

We're onto a middle-class couple who 'keep themselves to themselves' - apart from the multi-million-dollar drug ring they're running out of the family home. <Col: StageText>Raid their drug-packing operation</Col>.
Shit! The accounts have been frozen, but we can still sell the remaining diamonds. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Tigers <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>our smuggling <Col: StageText>office</Col>.

We busted the husband, but the wife's missing, as are the drug profits. Maybe she's holed up in the other property the couple own. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>their rented <Col: StageText>office</Col>.

Ah, crap. We got most of the diamonds out the back of the building, but there's one pack left in a courier vehicle. It's always the details! <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the 'Forcers <Col: StageText>retrieving the merchandise</Col>.
The Tigers just picked up the wife. She broke down and admitted that she was on her way to get her money laundered. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the dirty cash </Col>from her <Col: StageText>car</Col>.
The Tigers only have a small sample of our solitaires, but it's enough for a conviction. Stop them <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>the <Col: StageText>diamonds</Col>.
<Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>money</Col>. The wife transferred most of it to Colombian accounts but you have enough there to convict Mr. & Mrs. 'Nice Neighbors'.

What are we, diamond smugglers or scared newbies? When faced with a crappy jail sentence complete with the Tigers on the other side of the bars, I vote we fight! <Col: StageText>Blow up</Col> the Tigers!
Problem with these supposedly nice, respectable criminals is that they always mix with gnarly-looking dudes. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>planting bombs</Col> in the area.

The Enforcers have arrested our good friend Azrael. Okay, he is a bomb nut seeking to bring about the end of days, but he's still is a good laugh. <Col: StageText>Stop the 'Forcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding his house</Col>.

We have a crazed bomber in lockup, mumbling about angels delivering burning justice to San Paro. Whatever. <Col: StageText>Search his house </Col>and see if you can find some evidence against this nut.
Looks like Azrael was up to his old tricks. <Col: StageText>Guard his bombs </Col>and make sure the 'Forcers don't defuse them. We owe him for his good work in supplying our explosives.

Inside were incendiary devices and a list suggesting he has already planted some "righteous" <Col: StageText>bombs</Col>. Get to the first location and <Col: StageText>defuse the bomb </Col>while I bring forth a most furious justice.

The Enforcers are really leaning on our buddy Azrael and have discovered his bombing campaign. <Col: StageText>Guard his bombs </Col>and make sure they go off. Whoever Azrael is bombing, they deserve it.
The bomb nut demands to be called Azrael. He has confessed that there are two more <Col: StageText>bombs</Col>. Get to these locations and <Col: StageText>defuse them </Col>before anyone gets hurt.
Looks like 'Azrael' has some accomplices who may attempt to bomb these last two locations. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>planting these bombs </Col>.
Looks like our friend Azrael was bombing the supporters of a new gun ownership law. <Col: StageText>Plant bombs on the power supply unit </Col>to their campaign HQ and we can finish the job for him.
Bombing sure is fun, but it's time for something a little more personal. <Col:StageText>Take out the Enforcers</Col> that are trying to stop you.
The bomber has gotten away with this for the last time. <Col:StageText>Take him down</Col>, lethal force is authorized..
A plainclothes cop was seen scouting a car nearby. We think the vehicle is going to be used as part of a sting. <Col: StageText>Stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up that car</Col>.
Our drug enforcement arm need you to take point in an undercover sting operation. It's a San Paro classic: <Col: StageText>pick up this vehicle </Col>and use it to pose as a drug dealer.
Enforcers are in an undercover vehicle posing as drug dealers. Now they're cruising round our neighborhood looking for some action. <Col: StageText>Keep them away </Col>from our area.
<Col: StageText>Drive your vehicle into this area</Col>. Meanwhile, we'll contact some suppliers and see if they'll offer you some drugs to pick up.
A local scuzzball thought the undercover Enforcer was a bonafide dealer, and sold him some Angel Ace. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers</Col> from <Col: StageText>picking up the drugs</Col>.
A supplier has some Angel Ace he stole off his girlfriend... Bad boy. It's stashed it in an alley near your location. <Col: StageText>Pick up the drugs.</Col>
Now the Enforcers think our whole neighborhood is full of drug dealers. Their undercover guy is heading into this area to search for a dead-drop. <Col: StageText>Keep them out</Col>.
Okay, we've got some more calls to make. <Col: StageText>Drive your vehicle into this area.</Col> Keep your phone on - the drug pick-up should be close by.

The Enforcers have been sold a load of Goma Tabs, to be picked up. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>retrieving the drugs</Col>. They'll use this an excuse to get heavy in our neighborhood.

Next up, a job-lot of 'Nimbus', 'G-Sliders', and 'Goma Tabs'. The drop is in an alley near your location. <Col: StageText>Pick up the drugs</Col>. You play the part of an underworld scuzzbag well... Kinda worries me...

We can reclaim the honor of the neighborhood if we can <Col: StageText>stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the drugs </Col>back to their lockup! They'll use them to stereotype everyone here as a drug addict.
Man, this is just like picking candy offa kids. Especially if those kids went to Border High. <Col: StageText>Deliver the vehicle and drugs </Col>back to our lockup.

With all the Enforcer heat in the area, a dealer just bailed and abandoned a bag full of drugs and money. <Col: StageText>Retrieve and hold that bag</Col> - we can't just leave it out there! There are kids in this 'hood.

Those suppliers were so happy with you 'pushing so much product' that they want you to make a new pickup of drugs and money. Don't blow your cover: <Col: StageText>retrieve the bag </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>onto it.
There's an enforcer gang trying to Trick and Treat on our turf! That Candy is ours! We've several cameras in the are to discourage this, so <Col:StageText>Protect the Cameras</Col>.
We're going to do some trick or treating, but last year all we got was hollowpoint. <Col:StageText>Destroy the cameras</Col> to make sure any Enforcers don't spot us and give us a repeat this year.
There's an enforcer gang trying to Trick and Treat on our turf! That Candy is ours! We've several cameras in the are to discourage this, so <Col:StageText>Protect the Cameras</Col>.
We're going to do some trick or treating, but last year all we got was hollowpoint. <Col:StageText>Destroy the cameras</Col> to make sure any Enforcers don't spot us and give us a repeat this year.

They got the cameras, but not before they could determine which of the gang is the Trick or Treater! We don't know where he's going, but we have a lock on him. <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches all his targets.

The cameras spotted us, but we're not stopping.  Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the first <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
<Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches all his targets. We've no idea where he's going, so intercept him and take him down.
Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the second <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
<Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches all his targets. We've no idea where he's going, so intercept him and take him down.
Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the third <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
<Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches the last target. We've no idea where he's going, so intercept him and take him down.
Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the last <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
<Col:Opponent_Player>LAST STAGE!</Col>\nThe VIP has completed his Trick of Treating! <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> but make sure to <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>Stay Alive</Col>.

<Col:Opponent_Player>LAST STAGE!</Col>\nThe Trick or Treating is Complete! Protect the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> and <Col:StageText>Kill the Enforcers</Col> so we can go retire to gorge on candy.

Corporate spies have been hired to find the ingredients used in Mr. Clock's Corn Chips, and we need to stop them. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>electrical boxes </Col>which power our client's security grid.

The Enforcers seem whiter-than-white, but their allies are anything but: Valentine Foods have used toxic additives in their products for years to cut costs. <Col: StageText>Sabotage </Col>the <Col: StageText>power </Col>to their security.

Corporate spies have been hired to find the ingredients used in Mr. Clock's Corn Chips, and we need to stop them. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>electrical boxes </Col>which power our client's security grid.

The Enforcers seem whiter-than-white, but their allies are anything but: Valentine Foods have used toxic additives in their products for years to cut costs. <Col: StageText>Sabotage </Col>the <Col: StageText>power </Col>to their security.

The corporate spies are searching for the mildly addictive additives used in Mr. Clock products. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>additives </Col>from the spies and don't let them steal the information.

Now you've cut the power to Valentine Foods' security, we've got a chance to expose them and discredit the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Photograph </Col>the <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>that go into Valentine's 'Bio Snacker' products.

The corporate spies are searching for the mildly addictive additives used in Mr. Clock products. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>additives </Col>from the spies and don't let them steal the information.

Now you've cut the power to Valentine Foods' security, we've got a chance to expose them and discredit the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Photograph </Col>the <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>that go into Valentine's 'Bio Snacker' products.

The spies have what they need, but they must have gotten instructions to destroy our client's existing stock of ingredients. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>supplies </Col>from arson attacks.

Those photos are enough for the media to question who the Enforcers are really protecting: the people or the companies. For now though, <Col: StageText>burn </Col>those <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>to keep them out of circulation.
